segments.source: The live Slow Motion selector now has an October 13–Present roast-date period, newer than the periods available when this review was written. Match the date printed on the delivered bag to that selector before reading its component list; the accessible page shows multiple historical component pairs together, so assigning a displayed 50/50 pair to an unexamined bag would be false precision. The current page still says Swiss Water Process unless otherwise noted. This is a dated blend-record clarification, not Coffeedant tasting or an assertion that every retailer has the newest roast.

segments.source: Equator's current page gives a concrete immersion alternative to its drip and Chemex guides: a Fellow Clara press start of 45 g coffee to 675 g water, a stir at one minute and a plunge at four. That 1:15 method is a roaster recipe for a particular vessel, not a measured result from Coffeedant or an espresso yield. The same shop offers an 'espresso grind' purchase option but publishes no similarly specific espresso extraction target on this page. A press-first buyer has a reproducible start; an espresso-first buyer should choose whole bean and plan to dial in independently.

segments.source: The 18 g to 45 g espresso recommendation remains a roaster starting point for Decaf Black Cat, while the page's 'setting 1' applies to coffee ordered ground from Intelligentsia. It is not a universal home-grinder setting. Buy whole bean if you need to adjust grind for an unpressurized basket or switch between regular and decaf on one grinder; a fixed pre-ground selection cannot correct flow for your actual machine. No shot time, sensory result or dose suitability for every basket is established by the listing.

segments.source: Intelligentsia's current House page specifies a 1:18 filter starting ratio and recommends pour-over or automatic drip. Its '5 or 6' grind numbers describe the roaster's ordering scale, not a transferable dial setting for your grinder; use the coarse-salt texture cue only as a rough visual start. The same page currently identifies washed coffee from Lempira, Honduras, but that origin panel is a current lot record rather than a permanent guarantee. A filter-first household can begin with a small whole-bean bag and keep its own grind and dose notes before buying in bulk.

segments.source: Stumptown's present Trapper Creek method separates three jobs: a 28 g to 475 ml medium-coarse drip start, a 56 g coarse French-press dose with a four-minute press, and an espresso start around 19.5 g with a 23–28 second extraction. Its espresso output is given as about 1.5 fluid ounces, not a weighed beverage mass; use a scale and taste to establish a repeatable target in your own basket instead of silently converting volume to grams. One decaf can cover these methods, but changing grind and clearing retained regular coffee are part of that convenience claim. These are roaster instructions, not Coffeedant brews.
